main.title: TowerFall
main.subtitle: Four archers on the Ouya
main.summary: TowerFall debuted on Ouya in June 2013, before the later expanded Ascension releases.

cards.heading: The Ouya debut
cards.text: TowerFall is an action indie video game created by Maddy Thorson through her company Maddy Makes Games, which would later become Canadian developer and publisher Extremely OK Games. In the game, players control up to four archers in a multiplayer platform fighter. It was released on the Ouya microconsole in June 2013 and was later ported to PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Linux, OS X, and Windows as TowerFall Ascension and to the Nintendo Switch under its original title of TowerFall.

cards.heading: Targets, Trials and the additions in Ascension
cards.text: There are four game modes. In single-player, the player must hit targets around the arena before a timer runs out. The developer compared this mode to "Break the Targets" in the Super Smash Bros. series. Ascension adds a remodeled version of the target levels as a Trials mode, which requires the players to use power-ups to break all targets within several seconds. Ascension also adds a Quest mode, where one or two players attempt to survive against enemy waves of increasing difficulty. As a single-player event, Quest functions as a score attack mode. The new Ascension improvements were also released for the Ouya version.

cards.heading: A party game from a house of developers
cards.text: Local multiplayer tests in Thorson's Vancouver home helped shape TowerFall's party-game pace. Fellow developer Alec Holowka stepped back from the project after its game-jam beginnings but continued to help, demonstrating it at the 2013 Game Developers Conference and composing its music. After attention at PAX East, Thorson agreed with Ouya's Kellee Santiago to launch exclusively on the microconsole. MiniBoss supplied the finished graphics and Power Up Audio created the sound effects.

main.title: Rogue Legacy
main.subtitle: Each heir continues the exploration of the castle
main.summary: Rogue Legacy is a 2013 platform game with roguelike elements developed and published by Cellar Door Games.

cards.heading: Exploring a randomly generated dungeon
cards.text:
Rogue Legacy is a 2013 platform game with roguelike elements developed and published by Cellar Door Games. The game was released for Microsoft Windows, Linux, OS X, PlayStation 3, PlayStation 4, PlayStation Vita, Xbox One, Nintendo Switch, and iOS. A sequel, Rogue Legacy 2, was released on April 28, 2022 for Microsoft Windows, Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One.

The goal of Rogue Legacy is to explore a randomly generated dungeon, defeat four bosses in each of the four unique environments of the dungeon, and then defeat the final boss. Characters have the default ability to jump and slash with their sword, along with secondary abilities, such as magic attacks, which use mana. Players can also use their sword to slash platforms to make them extend.

cards.heading: Death gives way to a new heir
cards.text: Whenever a character dies as a result of losing all of their Hit Points (HP), control will transfer over to one of three randomly generated heirs which the player may choose between, though this number may be increased to six with a later upgrade. Each descendant carries their unique characteristics and abilities, including genetic peculiarities such as color-blindness (in which the game is presented in black and white), ADHD (in which the player moves faster) and dwarfism (in which the character is short and can fit into small gaps).

cards.heading: Gold improves the family inheritance
cards.text:
Gold found while exploring the castle can be used to improve the character's equipment and abilities, which are passed on to that character's heirs. Gold can be found by smashing pieces of furniture, opening chests, or defeating enemies. There are also various fairy chests hidden in special rooms throughout the castle, most of which require the player to complete an objective, such as taking no damage in the room, in order to be opened.

Spending gold on the manor, which appears after a new heir is chosen, can increase stats, such as health and mana, and unlock and upgrade new classes that may be carried by one of the heirs. These include mages, which can use more advanced spells, warriors, who have higher strength, and assassins, who can use various stealth techniques and have an increased likelihood of having a critical hit.

main.title: Dota 2
main.subtitle: Two teams of five heroes defend their Ancients
main.summary: Dota 2 is a 2013 multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) video game by Valve.

cards.heading: Ten heroes and two bases to defend
cards.text: Dota 2 is a 2013 multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) video game by Valve. The game is a sequel to Defense of the Ancients (DotA), a community-created mod for Blizzard Entertainment's Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos. Dota 2 is played in matches between two teams of five players, with each team occupying and defending their own separate base on the map. Each of the ten players independently controls a character known as a hero that has unique abilities and differing styles of play. During a match, players collect experience points (XP) and items for their heroes to defeat the opposing team's heroes in player versus player (PvP) combat. A team wins by being the first to destroy the other team's Ancient, a large durable structure located in the center of each base.

cards.heading: From Warcraft III mod to standalone game
cards.text: Valve hired Defense of the Ancients designer IceFrog in 2009 to develop a standalone successor. Dota 2 launched on Steam in July 2013 after a lengthy beta, with every hero available without purchase. Cosmetic items and related services support its free-to-play model. A 2015 update moved the game from Source to Source 2.

cards.heading: The International and the esports audience
cards.text: Dota 2 has a large esports scene, with teams from around the world playing in various professional leagues and tournaments. Valve organizes The International, the game's premier tournament which is held annually. Internationals feature a crowdfunded prize money system that has seen amounts in upwards of US$40 million, making Dota 2 one of the most lucrative esports. Media coverage of most tournaments is done by a selection of on-site staff who provide commentary and analysis for the ongoing matches similar to traditional sporting events. In addition to playing live to audiences in arenas and stadiums, broadcasts of them are also streamed over the internet and sometimes simulcast on television, with several million in viewership numbers.

cards.heading: Community, adaptations and OpenAI Five
cards.text: Despite criticism going towards its steep learning curve and overall complexity, Dota 2 was praised for its rewarding gameplay, production quality, and faithfulness to its predecessor, with many considering it to be one of the greatest video games of all time. It has been one of the most played games on Steam since its release, with over a million concurrent players at its peak. The popularity of the game has led to merchandise and media adaptations, including comic books and an anime series, as well as promotional tie-ins to other games and media. The game allows for the community to create their own gamemodes, maps, and cosmetics, which are uploaded to the Steam Workshop. Two spinoff games, Artifact and Dota Underlords, were released by Valve. Dota 2 has been used in machine learning experiments, with a team of bots known as the OpenAI Five showing the capability to defeat professional players.

main.title: Yo-kai Watch
main.subtitle: The creatures behind an ordinary day
main.summary: Yo-kai Watch is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing game about a child who gains the ability to see creatures responsible for everyday mischief. A special watch reveals the invisible Yo-kai living around Springdale, while the talkative Whisper explains this hidden world. Befriending its inhabitants produces medals that allow them to be summoned in battle. The adventure gives an ordinary neighbourhood another population to discover. Streets, homes and shops become places where a small human problem may have a supernatural character hiding just behind it.

cards.heading: The creatures behind an ordinary day
cards.text: Yo-kai Watch is Level-5's Nintendo 3DS role-playing game about a child who gains the ability to see creatures responsible for everyday mischief. A special watch reveals the invisible Yo-kai living around Springdale, while the talkative Whisper explains this hidden world. Befriending its inhabitants produces medals that allow them to be summoned in battle. The adventure gives an ordinary neighbourhood another population to discover. Streets, homes and shops become places where a small human problem may have a supernatural character hiding just behind it.

cards.heading: Six medals around a wheel
cards.text: A battle team contains six Yo-kai arranged around a wheel, with three active at a time. Rotating the wheel changes the group facing the enemy, making position and readiness part of the player's work while the creatures perform ordinary actions automatically. Touchscreen activities prepare special Soultimate moves, and other interventions help the team recover from trouble. The arrangement makes managing companions different from choosing every individual attack. A useful response can involve bringing a rested member forward or preparing the special action that the current situation needs.

cards.heading: Friendship begins with an encounter
cards.text: Exploring Springdale introduces Yo-kai through local incidents and side quests, giving their personalities a role beyond the battle roster. Food can help persuade a creature to become a friend, connecting items bought around town with the collection of new medals. Familiar companions such as Jibanyan give the hidden population a recognisable face. The appeal lies in returning to ordinary places with a new reason to look closely. A school day or a family disagreement can lead to another discovery, gradually filling the neighbourhood with memorable supernatural residents.

main.title: Mario & Luigi: Dream Team
main.subtitle: A holiday inside Luigi's dreams
main.summary: Mario & Luigi: Dream Team is AlphaDream's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure set on Pi'illo Island, where a holiday becomes a struggle involving Bowser and Antasma. Mario enters Luigi's dreams to help rescue the island's inhabitants, moving between the ordinary world and a side-on dream landscape. The brothers remain linked to separate buttons during their travels, but Luigi's sleeping imagination gives their partnership another form. The setting makes room for a great many Luigis at once, allowing a familiar supporting character to become the source of the adventure's most unusual possibilities.

cards.heading: A holiday inside Luigi's dreams
cards.text: Mario & Luigi: Dream Team is AlphaDream's Nintendo 3DS role-playing adventure set on Pi'illo Island, where a holiday becomes a struggle involving Bowser and Antasma. Mario enters Luigi's dreams to help rescue the island's inhabitants, moving between the ordinary world and a side-on dream landscape. The brothers remain linked to separate buttons during their travels, but Luigi's sleeping imagination gives their partnership another form. The setting makes room for a great many Luigis at once, allowing a familiar supporting character to become the source of the adventure's most unusual possibilities.

cards.heading: A sleeping face changes the landscape
cards.text: The touchscreen shows Luigi asleep while the upper display presents the Dream World. Interacting with the sleeper can affect the scene above: provoking a sneeze, for example, produces a gust of wind. Groups of Luiginoids can gather into forms that help Mario overcome obstacles, connecting the dream setting to a series of practical transformations. The controls make the connection visible across the hardware. A small action performed on Luigi below can change the space in which Mario needs to move, turning the two screens into different sides of the same dream.

cards.heading: Timing keeps the brothers involved
cards.text: Battles use turn-based choices with timed button presses to improve attacks or respond to incoming blows. In dreams, Luiginoids support Mario and supply larger Luiginary Attacks, while selected boss encounters turn Dreamy Luigi into a giant. The scale can change dramatically without losing the player's responsibility for the timing of an action. Dream Team extends the series through Luigi's identity rather than only another destination. His expressions, sleep and imagined duplicates provide both the comedy and the tools that make this particular journey possible.

main.title: Pikmin 3
main.subtitle: Three captains, new Pikmin and a search for fruit
main.summary: Pikmin 3 is a 2013 real-time strategy and puzzle video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii U video game console.

cards.heading: Alph, Brittany and Charlie explore PNF-404
cards.text:
Pikmin 3 is a 2013 real-time strategy and puzzle video game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii U video game console. It is the sequel to the GameCube games Pikmin (2001) and Pikmin 2 (2004), and it was released in Japan on July 13, 2013, with other regional releases following in July and August. Shigeru Miyamoto announced Pikmin 3 on July 16, 2008, for the Wii console, later stating at E3 2011 that it had transitioned to the Wii U.

The game builds upon existing elements of the Pikmin series, adding more player characters, Pikmin types, and support for Off-TV Play and downloadable content. In the single-player campaign, the player controls three alien captains: Alph, Brittany, and Charlie, who explore the surface of a planet they name PNF-404 in search of cultivable fruit seeds to save their home planet, Koppai, from famine. They befriend the Pikmin, who assist them in combat, solving puzzles, and gathering resources.

cards.heading: Rock Pikmin, Winged Pikmin and three captains
cards.text:
Pikmin 3 retains the Red, Yellow, and Blue Pikmin, and it also introduces two Pikmin types: the grey-colored Rock Pikmin, which can destroy tough barriers and are immune to being crushed by heavy objects; and the pink-colored Winged Pikmin, which can attack airborne enemies and travel through the air and over water. The game also retains the White Pikmin, which poisons enemies when eaten, and the Purple Pikmin, which have the strength of ten Pikmin, both of which are from Pikmin 2, but are only available in the side modes of this game.

The player controls up to three captains and switches between them to accomplish tasks and solve puzzles.

cards.heading: From Wii to Wii U: developing Pikmin 3
cards.text: A new Pikmin game was confirmed at E3 2008 during Nintendo's developer roundtable, in which Miyamoto stated that his team were working on a new entry in the series. Details concerning gameplay and development were left unmentioned. At Miyamoto's roundtable discussion at E3 2011, Miyamoto stated that Pikmin 3 development was moved to Wii U, the Wii's successor. He said that the Wii U's HD graphics and secondary-screen GamePad would work better for it.

main.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Dual Destinies
main.subtitle: A defence team returns to court
main.summary: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Dual Destinies is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS courtroom adventure bringing Phoenix back to legal practice alongside Apollo Justice and newcomer Athena Cykes. Its cases unfold during a crisis of confidence in the justice system, where fabricated evidence and wrongful accusations make the defence team's work increasingly urgent. Investigations gather the material used in hearings, and cross-examinations test the stories presented on the stand. Three playable lawyers give the connected cases different perspectives while preserving the series' pleasure of finding the detail that overturns a confident claim.

cards.heading: A defence team returns to court
cards.text: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney – Dual Destinies is Capcom's Nintendo 3DS courtroom adventure bringing Phoenix back to legal practice alongside Apollo Justice and newcomer Athena Cykes. Its cases unfold during a crisis of confidence in the justice system, where fabricated evidence and wrongful accusations make the defence team's work increasingly urgent. Investigations gather the material used in hearings, and cross-examinations test the stories presented on the stand. Three playable lawyers give the connected cases different perspectives while preserving the series' pleasure of finding the detail that overturns a confident claim.

cards.heading: Athena hears a conflicting emotion
cards.text: Athena's Mood Matrix analyses the emotions expressed during testimony. A witness may describe a frightening event while displaying an unexpected feeling, creating another inconsistency to investigate. The player identifies where the emotional response and the account fail to agree, then follows the resulting question. Phoenix's Psyche-Locks and Apollo's ability to notice nervous habits also return. Each technique supplies a different route through a guarded statement, adding to the evidence-based objections that remain the common foundation of the team's courtroom work across the connected cases.

cards.heading: A new stage for familiar gestures
cards.text: Dual Destinies introduces three-dimensional character models while keeping the exaggerated poses and sudden reactions central to the series' visual storytelling. Investigations allow locations to be examined for evidence before the case moves into court. There, pressing testimony can reveal additional statements, and presenting the relevant item exposes a contradiction. The more elaborate presentation supports the same practical rhythm: listen carefully, inspect what has been collected and recognise when two pieces of the story cannot both be true. A dramatic objection still depends on the player having understood a small detail.

main.title: Dragon's Crown
main.subtitle: Vanillaware’s painted adventurers and dungeons
main.summary: Dragon's Crown is a 2013 action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware for the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita.

cards.heading: Six classes search for the Dragon’s Crown
cards.text: Dragon's Crown is a 2013 action role-playing game developed by Vanillaware for the PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita. The game was published in Japan and North America by Atlus and in PAL regions by NIS America. A high-definition port for PlayStation 4, Dragon's Crown Pro, was released by Atlus in 2018. Players navigate environments from a side-scrolling perspective, choosing from six character classes to fight in the style of a beat 'em up and acquiring loot through repeated dungeon exploration. The storyline follows adventurers as they journey across Hydeland and become involved in the search for the magical Dragon's Crown.

cards.heading: Hydeland’s town and its establishments
cards.text: Dragon's Crown is a two-dimensional (2D) side-scrolling action role-playing game in which players take on the role of an adventurer exploring dungeons in the kingdom of Hydeland. The adventurer's base is a town at the kingdom's heart. There players interact with different establishments populated by friendly non-player characters (NPCs); the Adventurers' Guild where quests are accepted and the player can unlock new Skills; Morgan's Magic Shop where equipment can be repaired and upgraded; Canaan Temple, where players can pay to resurrect bone piles found in dungeons and receive boons for dungeon runs; and Lucain's Tower, which documents rune magic unlocked by the player.

cards.heading: George Kamitani revives the project
cards.text: Director and lead artist George Kamitani originally planned Dragon's Crown as a Dreamcast sequel to the 1997 Sega Saturn title Princess Crown. Following Vanillaware's successes with Odin Sphere and Muramasa: The Demon Blade, Kamitani restarted the project. Originally set to be published by UTV Ignition Entertainment, that company's withdrawal from the gaming market led to Atlus taking up the project. Upon release, Dragon's Crown received positive reviews from critics, who praised its gameplay and art style, while the story and repetitive elements drew criticism. The game also generated controversy for its exaggerated character designs and sexualized female characters. It had sold over one million units by September 2017.

main.title: Pocket Card Jockey
main.subtitle: Solitaire goes to the races
main.summary: Pocket Card Jockey is Game Freak's Nintendo 3DS combination of horse racing and a solitaire card game. A jockey's performance at the cards affects the progress of the horse, turning a familiar tabletop routine into part of a sporting contest. Between rounds the player chooses a position on the track, then builds toward the final stretch. The two activities continually feed one another. Clearing a line of cards is satisfying in itself, but its immediate consequence is that the horse and rider become better prepared for what is happening above.

cards.heading: Solitaire goes to the races
cards.text: Pocket Card Jockey is Game Freak's Nintendo 3DS combination of horse racing and a solitaire card game. A jockey's performance at the cards affects the progress of the horse, turning a familiar tabletop routine into part of a sporting contest. Between rounds the player chooses a position on the track, then builds toward the final stretch. The two activities continually feed one another. Clearing a line of cards is satisfying in itself, but its immediate consequence is that the horse and rider become better prepared for what is happening above.

cards.heading: Clear the cards and find a position
cards.text: The card game follows the golf-solitaire rule of selecting a card one rank above or below the current one. A good sequence clears the field while preserving cards in the deck, improving the unity between horse and jockey. Excess unity can become energy for the race. The touchscreen is also used to position the horse with the surrounding field in mind. These decisions give the cards a setting beyond the table: their result creates an opportunity, but the player still has to use that opportunity sensibly on the track.

cards.heading: A career continues through the stable
cards.text: Horses develop during a period of racing before reaching maturity, after which repeated losses eventually lead to retirement. Retired horses can breed, allowing a successful career to influence the next generation. The longer structure gives an unlucky race a place inside a wider attempt to build a capable stable. Pocket Card Jockey keeps those sporting ambitions approachable through its small, repeated card rounds. Each race offers another immediate puzzle, while the horse's growing history provides a reason to care about where the next run will leave it.

main.title: Killer Is Dead
main.subtitle: Combos, blood and a transforming gun arm
main.summary: Killer Is Dead is a hack and slash video game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture. It was released for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in August 2013 and for Windows in May 2014. It is published by Kadokawa Games in Japan, Xseed Games in North America and Deep Silver in Europe.

cards.heading: Mondo Zappa takes contracts around the world
cards.text:
Killer Is Dead is a hack and slash video game developed by Grasshopper Manufacture. It was released for PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in August 2013 and for Windows in May 2014. It is published by Kadokawa Games in Japan, Xseed Games in North America and Deep Silver in Europe.

Killer Is Dead is an action game where players take control of protagonist Mondo Zappa. As Zappa, the player goes through twelve story-driven missions selected from a world map; they range from short linear levels to longer levels that require exploration. Some level areas also require the activation of switches to move forward. During missions, Mondo fights a variety of enemies using his katana and cybernetic gun arm; using the latter changes the camera angle to an over-the-shoulder perspective.

cards.heading: Combos, blood and a transforming gun arm
cards.text: The combat of Killer Is Dead relies on maintaining the combo meter. Each time Mondo hits an enemy, he starts a combo chain which grows as long as Mondo lands consecutive hits without an enemy hitting him. At the highest combo level, special attacks are unlocked which provide different upgrade materials. Some enemies can only be finished off with a cinematic final attack, triggered once Mondo has absorbed enough blood from his enemies by chaining together combos. Mondo can both block and dodge attacks. Dodging plays to combat, as dodging at the right moment causes Mondo to enter Adrenaline Rush, where enemies are slowed and Mondo can land rapid attacks. Mondo's gun arm can transform into three gun types; the rapid fire "Bullet Shot" type, the "Freeze Shooter" which fires ice bullets to slow and even stop enemies, and the power "Charge Cannon" which deals higher damage when shots are charged up.

cards.heading: An assassin story with a distinctive visual identity
cards.text: Planning began in 2009, with full development following in 2011. Suda's title took inspiration from The Smiths' song The Queen Is Dead, while James Bond suggested the outline of a darker secret-agent story. His protagonist works in an underworld hidden from ordinary life. The team experimented with realistic graphics and a style recalling Killer7 before settling on its sharp cel-shaded appearance. Swords, guns and wrestling moves carry forward ideas from No More Heroes without making this a sequel. Against the bright tone of Lollipop Chainsaw, Suda described Killer Is Dead as a darker counterpart.
